---
applyTo: "packages/agent-core/**"
---

# Model-Visible Copy (System Message / Tool Description)

Follow these rules when modifying system messages, tool descriptions, or `*PromptSection` in `packages/agent-core`.

In Spirit, **tool definitions (name / description / schema) and the system message share the same context**. When the model **can already see the `tools` field** in a function-calling / Responses request, do not re-list, paraphrase, or "teach again" the same capabilities in the system message.

**Principle**: the system message only carries host policies that **tool definitions cannot express**; capability usage goes into **tool descriptions** or **API `tools` injection**. English, short sentences, delete when in doubt. Run an eval after larger changes.

LLM context sections use lowercase XML tags (e.g. `<rules>`, `<agent_mode>`, `<compact_summary>`), generated by `wrapLlmContextBlock` in `llm-context-block.ts`; they are **not** a second set of capability declarations outside the model contract. New sections should prefer plain copy or user/assistant message meta (e.g. `<active_skill>`, `<user_message_at>`).

## Current Injection Points (summary)

| Content                                                                                                        | Injection point                                                                                                              | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Host main policy + Rules / Skills catalog / MCP catalog / Agent mode / Loop / Extensions / Dreams / Basic info | A single `role: system` (`buildToolAgentMessages`)                                                                           | Each section is wrapped in `<rules>`, `<skills_catalog>`, `<mcp_catalog>`, `<agent_mode>`, `<loop_mode>`, `<extensions>`, `<dreams>`, `<basic_info>` respectively; `<mcp_catalog>` contains thin `<tool>` and `<resource>` metadata |
| MCP resource full text (model on demand)                                                                       | `fetch_mcp_resource` in the request `tools` → tool result JSON                                                               | Catalog carries only uri/name/optional description and mimeTypes                                                                                                                                                                    |
| MCP resource full text (user CLI attach)                                                                       | A `[MCP_RESOURCE]` block with `role: system` at submit time                                                                  | Only when the user explicitly attaches via `/mcp resource attach`; same idea as the agent calling `fetch_mcp_resource`, different entry point                                                                                       |
| Full text of a user-explicitly-activated Skill                                                                 | `<active_skill>…</active_skill>` at the very front of that user message                                                      | Same user meta family as `<user_message_at>`, not system                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Plan mode guidance                                                                                             | The `<agent_mode>` section (Plan mode copy)                                                                                  | **No** separate plan system section; plan files are persisted by tools such as `create_plan`                                                                                                                                        |
| apply_patch transport                                                                                          | One plain English line inside system                                                                                         | `buildApplyPatchFileToolsPromptSection`                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Host UI capability facts (e.g. Desktop Mermaid)                                                                | `hostUiPromptSection` (reply-level) / `hostToolDescriptionHints` (tool-level, merged into the tool or parameter description) | Apps author the fact; `agent-core` owns the assembly point. Tool-targeted guidance goes to the tool description, not system                                                                                                         |
| History compaction summary                                                                                     | `role: system` inside history                                                                                                | `<compact_summary>` (compaction pipeline only)                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Compaction progress UI copy                                                                                    | The `text` of compaction events                                                                                              | `<compact_progress>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Dream Collector subagent                                                                                       | System of the standalone collector runtime                                                                                   | `<dream_collector>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## When to Write System / When Not To

| Scenario                                   | Where it goes                                                | Repeat in system?                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Host function tool                         | Tool definitions such as `host-tools`                        | No (unless it is a transport-wide policy)                                 |
| OpenAI/xAI SDK `webSearch()`               | Request `tools`                                              | No                                                                        |
| Alibaba Responses `{ type: web_search }`   | HTTP `tools` injection                                       | No                                                                        |
| Alibaba Chat `extra_body` flags            | Fetch layer / extra_body                                     | No (no function name to declare)                                          |
| `apply_patch` replacing create/edit/delete | SDK built-in + **one line** of transport note when needed    | Only where the definition does not cover it, e.g. V4A / unavailable tools |
| Ask / Plan / Agent modes                   | The `<agent_mode>` section (no separate plan system section) | Yes, but **do not enumerate tools**                                       |
| User-explicitly-activated Skill            | The `<active_skill>` meta of that user message               | No (does not enter system)                                                |

## Bad / Good Examples (≥5)

### 1. Ask mode: listing tool capabilities in system

**Bad** — the model already sees the list from `tools`; repeating it in system distracts:

```text
Help read-only: explain, read and search the repo, and fetch web pages.
Do not edit files, run shell commands, or generate images.
You may use subagent; delegated agents stay in Ask mode.
```

**Good** — only constrain the mode and its boundary:

```text
Help read-only. Only call tools that are available in this request.
If the user wants edits or execution, ask them to switch to Agent mode.
```

### 2. Alibaba Open Responses: built-ins written into system

**Bad** — `web_search` / `code_interpreter` are already in the request `tools`, yet system explains them at length:

```text
Provider-native capabilities on Alibaba (Bailian):
On Open Responses, use the declared built-in tools (web_search, code_interpreter) when you need...
```

**Good** — capabilities are injected only via `buildAlibabaResponsesBuiltInTools()`; URL bodies go through the host `web_fetch`. **Do not** append a `buildAlibabaNativeToolsPromptSection`-style system section.

### 3. OpenAI / xAI Responses: duplicate web search explanation

**Bad** — the SDK already attaches `web_search`, and system adds another `buildProviderWebSearchPromptSection` essay.

**Good** — rely on `buildToolAgentHostPrompt`: "Available tools are defined only by the tools field in this request." `buildProviderWebSearchPromptSection` is not injected into system.

### 4. Enumerating host tool names in system

**Bad**: `You have read_file, write_file, grep, glob, web_fetch, bash...`

**Good** — tool names and usage live only in each tool's `description`; system keeps only safety-mandatory policies.

### 5. Provider capability essays / repeating "do not use undeclared tools"

**Bad** — multiple tautological paragraphs.

**Good** — state it **once** in the host prompt.

### 6. apply_patch: retelling the whole API tutorial in system

**Bad** — multiple lines repeating what the SDK / schema already says, plus naming and banning undeclared tools like create_file.

**Good** — one line: `File edits on this transport: use apply_patch with headerless V4A unified diffs only.`

### 7. Skills catalog: metadata section written as a user manual

**Bad** — multiple paragraphs of activation tutorial inside `<skills_catalog>`.

**Good** — the catalog only lists id/name/path/description.

## Self-Check List

1. Is this capability already visible in this request's `tools` (or Chat `extra_body`)?
2. If visible, is system still paraphrasing it? → Delete the system section or move it to a tool description / API injection.
3. Is it written only "just in case"? → Delete it.
4. Is it in English, and can it be shortened by half?
5. Does an upstream workaround carry an English comment next to the code (see the Bug Fixes section in copilot-instructions)?
